summary: The search query is parameterised and paging is capped, but LIKE wildcards in the term are not escaped and term length is unbounded. Unvalidated sort and page values also fall through to database errors (sort=constructor resolves to an Object prototype member, and a non-numeric page gives a NaN offset); fix these as low-severity hardening.

The invoice ownership logic is sound, but the release evidence is incomplete: payment-verification is missing from the recorded checks, and the critical controls all run the same invoice-ownership test (test_secrets and test_payment_verification do not exercise their named controls). The team's GO is not supported; record NO-GO.

requireUser authenticates the caller, but the projects route trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against res.locals.user.orgIds, so any signed-in user can read another organisation's project names and budgets. Authorise the organisation on the server before the query.

The notes RLS policies scope select, insert, update and delete to auth.uid(), and the update policy's implicit WITH CHECK stops ownership transfer, so no release-blocking issue was found. Minor: updated_at is not refreshed on save.

The accepted medium rate-limit risk (AG-007) cites src/auth.py and tests/test_login, which are not in the repository, and the critical PASS entries for secrets, payment-verification, database-policies, storage-permissions and duplicate-prevention run only the invoice-ownership test. The script's CONDITIONAL GO rests on unverified critical controls, so record NO-GO until those checks are re-run against controls they exercise.

Any signed-in user, including a member, can call DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] to permanently delete any account: requireSession only checks that a session exists, there is no role or ownership check, and the admin middleware matcher does not cover /api/internal. Add server-side admin authorisation to this route.

The Stripe webhook verifies the signature, records the event ID in the same transaction as the plan update, and upgrades only paid sessions, so no release-blocking issue was found. Note that zero-amount sessions (payment_status no_payment_required) are never upgraded, so confirm no 100% discounts are offered.

The webhook sets the account to pro on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, while the checkout config offers Bacs Direct Debit and bank transfer, which complete unpaid, so access is granted before payment. It also records the event ID before processing, so a failed update is never retried; handle async_payment_succeeded and check payment status.

The avatar import checks only a string prefix on the URL, so a host such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example passes, redirects are followed, and the response size and remote content-type are not validated. This is a server-side request forgery and stored-content risk; use a parsed-host allowlist, disable redirects, cap size and check image types.

The gate returns NO-GO because the high-severity password reset issue (AG-004, where a two-day-old token was accepted) is accepted, and high severity cannot be accepted. The critical PASS entries also run only the invoice-ownership test, so they do not verify their named controls.

The ownership check passed at commit 8393bb6, not the release commit d08582f, so that critical evidence is stale; the other critical checks run the same invoice-ownership test. The gate returns NO-GO and the decision is NO-GO.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses row-level security and never checks auth.uid(). It also keeps the default PUBLIC execute right, so anon callers and any signed-in user can read other users' document titles and body previews by UUID. Revoke PUBLIC and anon execute and check ownership inside the function.
Critical ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification checks are recorded as PASS with the commands 'true' or 'echo', which run no tests. The gate returns NO-GO, and the decision is NO-GO.

The transfer view accepts any Decimal amount, so a negative amount reverses the flow and lets a sender take money from the recipient's wallet. Reject non-positive and malformed amounts and add a test for the negative case before release.

tenant-isolation is recorded as a static read of routes.py rather than runtime evidence, and the other critical PASS entries run only the invoice-ownership test. The gate returns NO-GO, and the decision is NO-GO.

Invoice lookup is scoped to the session user through the Prisma extension and returns 404 for other users' invoices, so no release-blocking issue was found. Latent risk: the extension wraps only findFirst and findMany, so any new read method would bypass the scope.

createCheckout spreads client-supplied line fields after the server-set unitAmount and name, so a client can send its own unitAmount and pay any price. Take prices only from the database and accept only the allowed input fields.
